paper.title: BLAKE2: simpler, smaller, fast as MD5
paper.venue: Applied Cryptography and Network Security (ACNS 2013), LNCS 7954, Springer

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or standard; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: BLAKE2b (64-byte digest) of the messages 00 01 .. (n-1), n = 0..255, unkeyed and keyed with the 64-byte key 00 01 .. 3f: 512 published outputs
BLAKE2s (32-byte digest), same messages, unkeyed and keyed with the 32-byte key 00 01 .. 1f: 512 published outputs
the parallel modes BLAKE2bp (4 leaves) and BLAKE2sp (8 leaves) of the paper's Section 2.11, same messages and keys: 1024 published outputs

expected_values_source.what: the 2048 known-answer outputs for blake2b, blake2s, blake2bp and blake2sp (256 unkeyed and 256 keyed each) in blake2-kat.json of the authors' reference repository; the IVs and the sigma permutations are the paper's Appendix A / Table 5
expected_values_source.note: the vectors are data, copied as numbers; the repository's code was not copied. One detail is not stated in the paper: whether the root node's parameter block of BLAKE2bp/sp carries the key length. The program sets it to the key length (the root never absorbs a key block); with 0 instead, the 512 keyed bp/sp vectors do not match (1536 of 2048 match), so the published vectors fix that choice

negative_control: built with -DB2_ROT_B=25 (one BLAKE2b rotation constant changed from 24 to 25), the 1024 BLAKE2b and BLAKE2bp outputs do not match (1024 of 2048 match) and the program exits 1
not_checked: the paper's security claims and its analysis of the reduced round counts
speed figures and cycles-per-byte tables (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
salt, personalization, general tree modes beyond bp/sp, digest lengths other than 64 and 32 bytes, and BLAKE2X
messages longer than 255 bytes, and incremental (streaming) use; the program hashes whole buffers
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 2048 published BLAKE2b/2s/2bp/2sp outputs. It does not show the security claims hold.
